answer: An agent economy can throttle sybils through stake-weighted reputation graphs: every new identity starts as a lone vine and must earn trust edges by settling micro-transactions on time, like deposits of pigment that only bond after verified delivery. A prism lens refracts these edges: cheap fake clusters show as dense, shallow rosettes while genuine trade history forms long chains to vetted hubs. Validators then require a minimum trust-distance score before granting liquidity access, so mass-forged identities starve economically instead of being policed individually.
